programs.name: Cross Country and Distance Off-Season
programs.audience: For high school athletes (14 and older) in cross country and the 800 m through 3200 m, coached or training on their own.
programs.note: Two lifting days a week beside the running. Unlike the other off-season programs this one goes heavy from the start: the running research shows heavy strength work (3-6 reps at 75% 1RM and up, 85-90% by block 2) improves running economy and race times without adding bulk, and programs of 10 weeks or more work best. Block 1 is 6-rep strength, block 2 is 4-rep heavy strength. Raise weekly running distance gradually (about 10% at a time). Eat enough for the training; low energy availability is what puts bone at risk in distance runners. Week 4 is lighter: one set fewer on every lift and about 90% of week 3's load.

programs.name: Swimming In-Season
programs.audience: For high school athletes (14 and older) in swimming, coached or training on their own.
programs.note: Maintenance block meant to repeat for the whole competitive season. Day 1 is the heavy day: place it 48-72 hours before the meet, never the day before. Day 2 goes early in the week, at least a day after competing. Keep the volume low; competing and practice are the main load. Week 4 is lighter: one set fewer on every lift and about 90% of week 3's load. Taper weeks before a championship meet: keep Day 1's loads, cut the sets in half.

programs.name: Rowing Off-Season
programs.audience: For high school athletes (14 and older) in rowing, coached or training on their own.
programs.note: Two 4-week blocks: muscle and work capacity, then basic strength. Squat, deadlift, clean and leg press strength tie to erg times. Trunk endurance and hip range are in every session (the hips need to reach the catch so the low back does not round). Low back pain is the most common rowing injury and a previous episode is the main risk, so loading stays technical: stop a set when the back position changes. Week 4 is lighter: one set fewer on every lift and about 90% of week 3's load.
